description:
FILED s473b (Opus, 2026-09-07) from the #1010 probe battery.  PRE-EXISTING
(the same answer on 782bc37e); #1010 fixed the SLICE half of this rule and
deliberately left the ELEMENT half alone, because it is a different FORM
family and widening the same commit would have widened its blast radius.

    no warnings;
    { my %h=(a=>1); my @m = map {1} $h{zz};    print exists $h{zz} ? 1:0 }  perl 1  PCL 0
    { my %h=(a=>1); my @g = grep {1} $h{zz};   print exists $h{zz} ? 1:0 }  perl 1  PCL 0
    { my @a=(1);    my @m = map {1} $a[3];     print scalar(@a)         }  perl 4  PCL 1
    { my %h=(a=>1); my @s = sort {1} $h{zz};   print exists $h{zz} ? 1:0 }  perl 1  PCL 0

The three that already AGREE, and they show the mechanism is present:

    { my %h=(a=>1); for ($h{zz}) { }           }  perl 1  PCL 1
    { my %h=(a=>1); my $r = \$h{zz};           }  perl 1  PCL 1
    { my %h=(a=>1); sub f {} f($h{zz});        }  perl 0  PCL 0   <- LAZY, correctly

THE CAUSE is one missing consumer in the emitter's lvalue-context table.
`Pl::ExprToCL::_elem_accessor` picks `p-gethash-box` (EAGER: creates the key)
when `lvalue_context` is set, `p-gethash-argbox` (LAZY defelem) under 'argbox',
and a plain `p-gethash` otherwise.  A foreach list and a `\(â¦)` set the
context; the map / grep / `sort BLOCK` LIST arguments do not, so their element
reads lower to the plain accessor:

    for ($h{zz}) {}      ->  (p-foreach ($_ (vector (p-gethash-box %h "zz"))))
    map {1} $h{zz}       ->  (p-map (lambda ($_) 1) (p-gethash %h "zz"))       <- here

map and grep ALIAS $_ to each element (that is why `map { $_ .= "!" } @a`
writes through), so they belong with foreach, not with join.

THE FIX SHAPE, and why it is not two lines: the three list arguments are
generated in ExprToCL, so the cheapest correct change is to set
`lvalue_context(1)` around the LIST argument of map / grep / sort-with-a-block
â but only where the argument is an element access, the way `_is_elem_arg`
gates the 'argbox' path per argument (a blanket context leaks into arbitrary
subtrees; the comment at `_is_elem_arg` records a `~$_` method argument that
flipped from string- to numeric-complement under exactly that mistake).
ALTERNATIVELY, extend #1010's `%p-aliasing-slice-form` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp)
to rewrite an ELEMENT read as well â the p-map / p-grep compiler macros are
already there and would need one more clause â which keeps the whole rule in
ONE place at the cost of a runtime-side element rewrite.  Measure the emission
blast radius (`tools/corpus-diff.pl`) before choosing: `map { â¦ } $h{k}` is
rarer than `map { â¦ } @list`, so it should be small.

`sort` is the odd one and must be probed separately BEFORE it is included:
a single ELEMENT under `sort BLOCK` vivifies in perl (row 04 above) while a
SLICE under `sort` does NOT (`my @s = sort @h{'a','zz'}` leaves the keys
absent, probed at #1010 â that is why #1010's negatives include sort).  Do not
assume the two halves agree; they do not.

BAR when taken: the probe table above vs perl 5.40.3, a guard row beside
#1010's in Pl/t/autoviv-02.t (rows 14/15 are the slice halves), corpus-diff
with every differing file explained, and the full sweep (perl's own for.t
carries a TODO row on this family â see the s473b note in
baselines/pass-baseline.tsv).
subject: A single ELEMENT consumed by map/grep (and `sort BLOCK`) does not vivify â `map {1} $h{zz}` leaves the key absent where perl creates it; the ELEMENT twin of #1010, which fixed the SLICE half
